newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Former Afghan govt forces launch assault on Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Former Afghan govt forces launch assault on Taleban.

text.p: Forces belonging to the ousted Afghan government launched an attack on Sunday using rockets, heavy artillery and warplanes in an attempt to dislodge Taleban troops from a strategic pass north of Kabul.
Shells and rockets landed every minute around the De Sabz pass, 30 km (20 miles) north of the Afghan capital, kicking up dust in the barren mountains.
"We are very busy now," General Abdul Rauf Begi, commander of forces at the frontline belonging to northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, told reporters.

Wearing the faction's trademark olive-green kepi, or cap, Begi sat in the turret of a mud-walled compound in Tutakhon, around 50 km (35 miles) north of Kabul, directing fire over a walkie-talkie and glancing at a Russian-printed map in front of him.
A uniformed orderly offered a tray of grapes to the commanders gathered round the general.
Dostum's troops have joined forces with those of the former Afghan government's military chief, Ahmad Shah Masood, to try to drive the radical Islamic Taleban militia out of Kabul.
The Afghan capital fell to Taleban troops a month ago on Sunday, giving the group control of over two-thirds of the war-torn country.
According to Masood's commanders, the assault began at 6 a.m. (0130 GMT), with warplanes from Dostum's air force making two sorties over Taleban positions early in the morning.
"They (Dostum aircraft) bombed twice this morning," said Sayid Akbar, one of Masood's commanders on the road before Tutakhon.
"The Taleban only have one position left," he said, adding fighting around a second pass, Khair Khana, was less intense.
A jeep with a multi-barrelled rocket launcher mounted on the back sped down the road towards the front, the chequered cloths around the soldiers' heads flapping in the wind.
There was sporadic return fire from Taleban forces, who shelled former government positions in the middle of the desolate plain below the De Sabz pass.
According to a senior former government official, the Taleban still hold the road on the pass.
An assault launched by former government forces last week was stalemated, with the Taleban remaining on the pass despite a shower of rockets and shells.
"Our (Masood's) forces and Dostum's are much better coordinated today," said the senior former government official.

Just before 10 a.m. (0530 GMT) on Sunday, Reuters cameraman Des Wright saw a Taleban jetfighter bomb close by General Begi's headquarters and close to where his heavy artillery and rocket launchers were firing.
At around 10.30 a.m. (0600 GMT), witnesses said a Taleban plane bombed the town of Jabal Os-Siraj, where Masood's headquarters are located, around 90 km (60 miles) north of Kabul.
"Five people were lightly wounded," said a representative with the aid organisation, Medecins Sans Frontieres.
